# Chapter Four: City in the Trees

Corliss sat there staring at the large hole that still glowed blue from the cannon ball that had landed there. “Where did thy get those from?” she asked shaking her head. Most of the wardens, well over one half were still getting treated for wounds well those that didn’t die, they were down to ten, ten senior wardens and a handful of initiates, one night and there order had taken a blow that was close to ending it she thought still staring at the large hole.

“I have seen them, but that was two years ago on a visit to the capital, they were still a prototype then, I guess the Empress put them into production, this does not bode well for Lusor or Dever” Uri said standing above her. “Yeah it wasn’t exactly a picnic for us either Uri, this place is done” she said looking around at what was left of the old abby. The walls were gone, except for one or two large sections the rest had been reduced to so much rubble, the main building no longer stood neither did the stables or the bunkhouse, at least, thankfully she thought they had gotten the horses out before the building had been hit.

Uri looked around the area himself and Corliss could see the troubled expression on his face. “We will need to leave, at least one scout got out and if so then they will report to the Lord Seer at Warden’s keep, if they bring anything close to the size of that small scouting platoon, then we will be done” he finished and Corliss winced He was right they had no more cover, most of there people were at best walking wounded. Even the Silvan had taken heavy losses. Not one group escaped this battle without heavy casualties.

Corliss surveyed the wounded, “we should have left for Castello a day ago Uri, we can’t stay here too much longer” she began “There is nothing we can do here, this place is no longer safe, worse before long every enemy in the area will know we are here, if we stay. We will die, fight honorably and give the enemy losses, but die none the less” she finished. Corliss looked at Uri and could see those calculating eyes going to work as he reguarded the other man.

Durass came to join the two, his people had finished packing up the wounded as Uri turned to him “If we do go with you, how will we be received?” Uri asked, the question sounded casual, but she had known her mentor long enough to sense the underlying seriousness of the query. Durass seemed to as well he was silent as he reguarded the older man “You will be guests Uri, that is all, I will not bind your honor to serve us nor will I ask you to ally yourselves with my people. I know you serve the crown, despite the last few weeks I know you still hope the crown will be saved and you can go back to doing what you love. So, Uri will you and your people be my guest?” Durass asked and the old bear of a man smiled at him. “Yes General, I would be honored”. With that the plan was settled, they began to pack up what little remained and prepared the wounded for traveling. The precession left before the sun rose as the winding snake of lights began to acend the paths into the Barrens, a place that most had never traveled. The wardens and Silvan spread out guarding the wounded and the refugees, most of those who had come running from the tyranny of the Empress now walked wide eyed and frightened into a place that until that moment had only been myth and rumor.

They walked for most of the day, finally setting up camp along the worn hunting paths. That night was uneventful as the group rested, the only sound aside from the moans of the wounded were the chirps and screetches of the forest creatures as they came out to hunt for food. Starting out early the next day the precession walked, stopping only to eat along the trail.

Corliss stood out front of the group running point with Durass and Uri, As she studied the trees and plants she began to notice odd markings along some of the trunks Durass noticed her looking and smiled “Its our way of marking where you are, its also how we find our cities and villages, without publicly advertising them” he said. Corliss studied the symbols and then turned back to the slight man. “You have planned for a war with the territories for a long time haven’t you?” she asked and Durass’s face transformed into a surprised look. “You are very observant, we have not planned for it, but felt that sooner or later it was inevitable, so yes we have ensured the ability to secure our lands without making it easy for lowlanders to invade” he finished nodding approvingly at her. She thought about this for a while, true they had a treaty but that treaty was the equivalent of ‘stay on your side and I will stay on mine’ and with that kind of message, it would be easy to assume that tensions would rise at some point and with little ability to communicate it was inevitable that war would break out she thought, that was until this, until the Empress forced her own people into slavery and the only salvation was into the arms of those whom they had only heard stories about.

Walking along the trail she had gotten so used to the close trees and protective brush along the sides that when it opened it it nearly startled her, but it was the sight above that truly put her in awe. Rising from the expanse of forest below was a series of large trees climbing into the sky, all five of them set into a ring formation, but it was near the top that held the truly amazing sight. Nestled above them was the buildings and profile of a city within the trees. “I have never seen anything like it” Corliss breathed extending her eyes upward to reguard the amazing sight. Within the expanse of the five trees it looked as if someone had built a base of wood, reinforcing it they then set buildings in a grid pattern, surrounded by ornate bannisters along the edges, and as if that weren’t enough they then did it again, giving a two story city within the forest hanging well above the ground. “How was this even done?” Corliss continued trying to take in the ornate carved animals carved into support pillars every twenty feet or so as well as the architecture of the buildings, where the villages of the south were utilitarian, these were more artform then housing she thought. Decorative trim and circular rooms adourned the normal square shapes of what would be a store or house. Durass smiled with pride as he watched the group of low landers reguard his city. “It happened over multiple generations, we are a people who are more comfortable within the trees so we lived for a long time building small houses within a tree, but after a while he began to design and build entire cities off of the ground, it took a lot of work and even more engineering but this is not the only nor is it the biggest city we have, but I am glad you find it amazing” he said, motioning for them to follow.

They walked to the base of the ariel city, Corliss was finding it hard to keep her eyes on the ground so she wouldn’t trip as they kept rising to inspect the amazing feat of engineering above her. The precession came to stand in the shadow of the city, coming to one of the large trees as they gathered around Durass. “Entering our city makes you our guests” he began raising his voice to ensure everyone heard him. “However that comes with some rules, you are free to venture around the city, we ask that you respect people’s privacy and obey the orders of the guards, we will do our best to find you lodging, but it might take a while, until then you will be staying in our commune hall, it is not the most comfortable place, but its all we have until we can find you better accomodations” he finished and everyone nodded, though more in show and awe at the sight of the city then anything else. Durass nodded once he was complete his small speech, walking over to one of the largest trees, Corliss finally noticed an ornate set of doors carved into it, it was one of the most beautiful things she had ever seen and must have taken a decade to complete from the detail, the wood had at one point been two solid pieces that someone had carved out to look like whisps of smoke as unicorns and dragons danced through it, it was breathtaking Corliss thought studying the two doors until they opened, the inside of the tree was hollow.

Stepping onto the bottom of the trunk stained dark but still displaying rings they waited until the ringed floor began to rise, Gasps went out from the twenty people standing inside including Corliss “What is this?” she breathed, wondering if a mage had begun to float them up Durass just smiled.

“We have spent years working on things you lowlanders had long forgotten, this is a small steam engine that hauls metal ropes attacked to this cab to pull us up” he finished, and Corliss could hear the pride in his voice. The cab as Durass had called it rose evenly almost gliding she thought, small metallic whines muted by the walls sounded outside the cart. Desipte the man’s reassuring grin sweat broke out over her body as she imagined rising in this little box towards the city well above the ground. But she kept that to herself, instead concentrating on keeping her face calm.

Finally, mercifully the cab came to a stop and the doors slide open, light streaming in as a crowd appeared beyond at first she wasn’t sure what to make of it, but then realized that most of th elven hadn’t seen people in a long time, most stood there gawking or whispering to one another until the booming voice of General Durass sounded over the caucaphony of voices “Medics, NOW, clear the commons, that’s an order” he yelled as his voice echoed over the area.

As the last echo began to fade people began moving out, some on their own, others herded by guards in armor. Replacing them were a group of elven dressed in light purple, walking with purpose and authority they approached the elevator. Durass began moving people out of the cabin, putting those wounded to the left where they were intercepted by the Silvan group all dressed in purple. “Is this all” came one voice, an elder Silvan looking to Durass who lowered his eyes and shook his head.

“Unfortunately, no, there will be more” he said, ushering all out of the cabin and Corliss found herself walking out onto an ornate wooden floor, the different shades of wood making patterns and as she looked noticed paths like sidewalks out of the interlocking wood. Buildings surrounded the common area and here, this close the detail was breathtaking yet again. Carvings of wood and crystal covered the front of every building, it was almost too much to take in Corliss thought as the doors shut behind her and she heard the cab wind its way down again to retrieve even more people. Surveying the area, she noticed something that made her stop and look twice, there was a giant fountain as the centerpiece of the common area, as water poured fourth from the mouths of metal carved fish and crystal waves. The artisans that the Silvan had created had no equal among the low landers she thought trying to process every piece of building and floor, every carving which not only were detailed but looked incredibly realistic, as if someone had turned animals into wood, propping them up along the fronts of buildings and long paths as statues. It as the most amazing thing she had ever seen. “Warden, please gather Uri, you will need to come with me” Durass said and his tone was serious enough to break her out of her trance.

From his tone the fate of there ability to stay there weighed heavily on whatever meeting they needed to attend she thought and nodded at Durass as he continued to help with the wounded. Two full cabs later Uri finally emerged, gawking like a schoolboy and Corliss had to surpress a smile, she had probably looked the exact same way upon entering this common area. “My Lord, we are being summoned” she said, making her tone serious and sharp, he popped out of his own trance, sensing the seriousness of her request. Leveling the old stone gaze at her, he nodded once and Durass came over to the two them.

“We do not have permission to be here, we will need to talk to the council, understand they have the power to expell you, I apologize but there was no way to talk to them ahead of time, however because I have invited you, they need to hear you and vote before they can take an action, my honor is now at stake, and that is something we take very, very seriously. “He finished and the two followed as Durass began wading through the growing crowd on the commons area, Corliss looked up and was amazed as Silvan youth jumped from branch to branch trying to get a better look at the strangers below.

Building after building was even more amazing as they crossed out of the common area and entered what looked like a main street, ornate wooden signs hung outside shops advertising leather goods, crystals, weapons and more as they walked down the interlocked wooden boulevard. Silvan’s making way as Durass strode with confidence down the center of the street. She spied a metal basin as one woman hung her head drinking from water running out of a spout and then disappearing down into the basin. Pointing it out to Uri he looked and nodded smiling, enjoying her marvel at the technological marvels of these people.

Finally at the end of the boulevard the street opened into yet another common area, except across the wide space stood a three story building with four large smooth treetrunks as pillars that held a triangle shaped roof, in the center of the triange was an ornate crystal design that pulsed and swirled as if it had a life of its own. Climbing the smooth wooden steps, they came to another set of large ornate double doors. The building had the look of something official Corliss thought but it was unlike anything she had ever seen in Vicor. Where all the official buildings were keeps or large stone castle like structures, the entire city here had been carved from the forest, not an ounce of stone, only crystal, wood and some metal. She had never seen its like and decided unless she returned here, she never would again.

The two large doors opened slowly as a man appeared, dressed again in that long robe, this one was white complete with a white scarf that hung nearly to the floor. The man bowed low Durass. “General Durass, champion of the huris invasion, tip of the spear during the lostric campaign, honored holder of the wood soldier and two leafs for bravery” called the man. Durass stood their stalwart as theman regailed them with the titles earned by the seasoned General.

“You come before the council of Lapis to ask for judgement reguarding the outsiders” the man said, it wasn’t a question and Durass still did not speak. Finally, them looked over Uri and Corliss, he did not bow, nor did he smile after a moment his eyes quickly dismissed them as if they were not worth the time to speak to. Corliss could see the flash of annoyance on Durass’s face and finally he did speak, ensuring his voice was loud enough that the onlookers who had begun to gather at the base of the stairs could hear. “Honored Seargeant at Arms, I am here to ask the council’s indulgence to allow those I have invited, on my honor to be our guests for a time so that we may learn all we can about the lowlands, disturbing things are happening and they may effect us, these honored guests not only may hold answers that we may need, they also have fought bravely alongside my own men to help defend lowlanders and Silvan’s alike.” He finished, the Seargent seemed almost shocked at this admission and for a moment Corliss had to hide a smile, the pompous ass had no idea what to do and he had been rendered speechless for the moment. She could guess that did not happen often.

After a pregnant silence the Seargant at Arms seemed to regain his composure “I shall ask the council if they wish to indulge your highly inappropriate invitation and request” he finally stammered out, quickly disappearing into the large hall. Once the Seargeant had disappeared into the building and the doors had closed behind him. Durass came to stand next to the two Wardens. He kept the smile on his face but Corliss could hear the anxiety in his tone as he spoke through the smile plastered there like armor from the crowds as they continued to grow in the commons area, everyone seemed to have their eyes on Corliss and Uri and she could feel every single pair of eyes gawking and whispering as they stared unabashedly at them. “When we go in, do not speak unless one of the councils speaks to you, no matter what is said, do not argue or raise your voice, allow me to do the talking” he finished, and both nodded once to him

They had waited outside for what seemed like an eternity as the crowd doubled in size the whispers sounding like the ocean as it blasted against canyon rocks and then withdrew she thought trying to make out any one of the voices but unable to in the caucaphony of whispered sound. Finally the doors opened and the robed Seargeant exited the door, this time carrying a long wooden staff, coming to stand in the center of the large porch, he looked around at the growing crowd and Corliss caught a nervous glance and then it was gone, replaced with the air of authority and calm. Raising the large staff, he beat it against the ground three times. He waited for a moment, but the whispers didn’t quite all die down, this time an annoyed expression flashed over his face before he once again beat the staff three times slowly against the wood of the raised dais.

The crowd finally went quiet, every eye turned to him as he stood there looking over the gathered people. He is enjoying this Corliss thought seeing the small smile on his face as he surveyed them, allowing the quiet to extend in fact it could be said that he was creating the theatrics for this moment she thought. Having seen many a seer, lord, noble and advisor do the same within the navigation of her own people’s politics, it was almost reassuring to know that despite their differences, they were still a lot of similarities.

“General Durass, you may enter with your charges, however you will be held responsible, on your honor for there actions. Do you agree to these terms” the Seargeant stated, again loud enough for all to hear? Durass aloud the silence to play out as well for a moment longer then he needed to. “I accept these terms, however these two have shown an abundance of honor and would stand on their own, should the council allow”. There was a gasp from the crown, and she could see the shocked look on the Seargants face. Corliss wasn’t sure what Durass had said wrong, but she knew taboo when she saw it. “General Durass, lowlanders are not known to have honor, it would be an affront to this hall to attribute such to them” the Seargant said almost chiding the General.

Corliss wasn’t sure what was going on, but from the look it was important and moreso, important for the outcome of this meeting she thought, not answering but just continuing to watch the drama play out on the dais. “Would you say the person who saved my live and the lifes of more then ten of our Silvan Warriors without reguard for their own life or safety one without honor or bravery” Durass spoke, again loud enough for the entire crowd to hear. Corliss could hear the mock shock and dissapointement in his voice. She was starting to understand, honor was everything with these people it seemed. To have them enter on their own honor would make it harder for the council to so easily dimiss them she surmised, trying her best to hid a smile as Corliss watched the Seargent practically choke on his own words. “I will consult with the council on this” he stated and practically ran back into the building.

Looking over she saw Durass, he turned to ensure one side of his face was hidden from the crowd and winked at them. Again, Corliss surpressed a smile trying to maintain a serious and sedate gaze. Trying to best to play along with a game she was unfamiliar with. The Seargant returned, this time not bothering to come unto the dais, opting instead to simply motion for them to enter. Durass went first followed by Uri and Corliss brought up the read. Entering the large single room of the chambers she saw the large platform constructed in a semi circle, twelve black robed members an even mix of men and women sat atop the raised platform, giving them an air of authority and superiority. Corliss knew nobles when she saw them and nodded to herself, another thing they had in common she thought.

The small group came to stand in the center of the room, looking up at the group. “General Durass” began one woman looking the small group over as she spoke. “You come before us, asking this body to take these two lowlanders on their own honor and ask us to bestow guest status on them and there group, you do this based on your claim they have saved you and your warriors when you were unable to do so yourself.”

She continued pausing for a moment before locking eyes with the General a small smile on her face “Are you saying that these lowlanders are better warriors then you and your brethren?” She said pushing at the General who did his best to hide a smile on his own face. Corliss was trying to understand what exactly was taking place here, it was almost like they were sharing a private joke. “Councilor, I do not make that claim, only that at a time when my warriors where entrenched these two lowlanders took it upon themselves, risking their own lives to aid us when they could have simply retreated, I do admit however that had they not, my warriors were more then capable of defeating the enemy, however this speaks to their own moral fiber then my soldiers prowess in battle” he finished smoothly and the councilor nodded to him, as if this were a debate and he had just won a point.

The twelve members of this body nodded to each other as they whispered among themselves until one stood, shooting an angry and annoyed gaze at Durass “How dare you come into this chamber, claming lowlanders have honor, that’s an offront to this body of government and these hallowed halls, I call a vote to immediately dismiss these … people from our sight and lands at once” the councilor yelled, slamming his fist on the table in front of him for emphasis. Durass simply reguarded him cooly as the man continued to standing there, looking from one member to the next trying to see if he had the support for such a vote and quickly realized he did not. “Esteemed councilor, are you questioning my honor, or more importantly accusing me of lying to our most honored governing body?” Durass asked, his tone was low and there was an edge to it, Corliss knew enough that if this man said yes, Durass would kill him where he stood. The entire council went quiet, as a few looked from Durass to the councilor who still stood. His bronze face going white as his large eyes went even wider, soenthing that Corliss didn’t think was possible. He quickly stammered out apologizies to Durass, she wasn’t sure, but Corliss thought that might have been a duel challenge that the man had narrowly escaped from.

The session went on for two more hours, the councilor’s going back and forth, asking Durass to explain in detail the honor shown by the low landers, some councilers getting up and stating that it has been scientifically proven that low landers do not demonstrate honor or fealty.

Finally the council had deliberated for another hour coming back they made the judgement that it was indeed possible for lowlanders to display honor, but since it could not be documented, they would abstain from entering that into the official record, however the lowlanders could stay and Durass would be responsible for there behavior on his honor. The angry councilor from earlier clearly stating that Durass’s honor was unquestioned and the entire council felt that his was strong enough to survive even the lowlanders should they misbehave.

Once the ass kissing was done Corliss thought, they were allowed to go, as they left the chambers the Seargent handed them each a robe, magenta, this was to be worn while in the city as a mark of visitation he said as if that explained it fully. Durass motioned for them to follow and they exited the large building and began to walk back towards the elevator to try and organize the wardens and initiates.

As they walked, he looked at the robes and smiled “My People take the duties as host very seriously, its almost a competition, as a guest you are a person of honor, even being lowlanders” he said chuckling at the evil eye Corliss shot him. “It’s a mark of honor to outdo others in ensuring you feel comfortable and are shown generosity” he finished and just as he ended the explanation two Silvans approached each holding a large wooden plate of fresh fruit, with a bow they offered the contents to Corliss and Uri, who partook of a few pieces, thanking the two Silvans and catching up to Durass. “I don’t know General; I think I am going to like it here” she said smiling.

Once they returned the three of them went about securing lodgings for everyone, ensuring the wounded were looked after and someone was present at the hospital should the doctors need questions answered. By the time they were done, the sun had set and the crystal lanterns began to glow along the common area, the effect was one of the most beautiful things Corliss had ever seen, her breath caught in her throat as the wooded floor and buildings were awash with blue, pink, purple and red lights as lightning bugs danced just above the floor like small ghosts of forest creatures come to visit there Silvan brethren. They stood there, enjoying the night air and the scene for nearly thirty minutes until with a resigned sigh Durass motioned for them to follow.

They walked down a few residential streets, these buildings still decorative but muted compared to the markets and common areas. They came to a two story dark wood house and entered, Inside it was an expansive room divided into a living area and kitchen with a row of stairs leading to a loft above and then another set to an entire floor above that, the wood rafters and waynscotting giving the room a very earthy look Corliss thought.

Durass waved them over and pulled out maps from below the desk, spreading them out Corliss could see it was the area around the city and even went as far as to show the old Abbey. “This is what we are up against, the Empress is declaring war, the question is, will she declare it on the barrens. If the rumors of a Lord Seer taking over the Wardens keep are true then that answer is yes and we are going to need to come up a plan, otherwise this very city could be the victim of the Empresss subjugation Uri” he said his tone serious and uri returned the stare. The three got to work try to anticipate attacks and plan defenses.
